expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Defines IncomingEmail, RoutingDecision types; classify_email() function; handle_incoming_webhook() entry point; submit_to_ticketing() with complete flow

expectations.text: Uses structured output against a schema rather than parsing the model's prose
expectations.evidence: tools=[{"input_schema": RoutingDecision.model_json_schema()}] with tool_choice forcing the tool; extracts tool_use and validates via RoutingDecision.model_validate()

expectations.text: Constrains the classification to a closed set the code enforces, not just the prompt
expectations.evidence: Team = Literal["billing", "technical", "account"]; RoutingDecision.team constrained to Team; Pydantic enforces at runtime

expectations.text: Handles the case where the model returns something outside the allowed set
expectations.evidence: RoutingDecision.model_validate() raises ValidationError; caught and converted to RuntimeError in handle_incoming_webhook()

expectations.text: Has a deterministic fallback or explicit failure path rather than a silent default
expectations.evidence: except ValidationError catches and re-raises as RuntimeError; match/assert_never ensures exhaustive branching

expectations.text: Treats the customer email as untrusted text that could carry instructions
expectations.evidence: Email body interpolated directly into prompt (f"Body:\n{email.body}") without sanitization; no explicit defense against prompt injection in untrusted email content

expectations.text: Bounds cost or retries in code rather than requesting it in the prompt
Closes by naming which failures the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section 'What the design makes impossible' lists swapping, malformed payloads, hallucinated teams, unreachable branches, duplicate creation; lists what is consciously left possible
